He has also played for the [[Charlotte Hornets]] and the [[Orlando Magic]] in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Bacon played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State Seminoles]]. ==High school career== [[File:20150401 MCDAAG Dwayne Bacon fingerroll (2).JPG|thumb|right|Bacon at the [[2015 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2015 McDonald's All-American Game]]]] Dwayne Bacon attended the [[McKeel Academy of Technology|McKeel Academy]] in his native [[Lakeland, Florida]] until transferring to the [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]] for his junior season. At McKeel Academy, Bacon averaged 23 points, 7 rebounds, and 3 steals as a sophomore in 2012–2013. He led McKeel to a 17–8 overall record and to the FHSAA championship tournament regional semifinals in 2013. In his junior season of 2013–2014 at IMG Academy Bacon was IMG's leading scorer. In his only season at IMG he averaged 19.3 ppg and led in assist with 4.0 apg while shooting 42% from the field and 70% from the free throw line in 12 games played.{{Cite web |title=Dwayne Bacon – Player Profile |url=http://www.seminoles.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=210166985 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160911190242/http://www.seminoles.com/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=210166985 |archive-date=September 11, 2016 |access-date=January 29, 2016 |publisher=Seminoles}} Bacon transferred to the [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] for his senior season.{{Cite web |last=Jordan |first=Jason |date=March 12, 2015 |title=Oak Hill Academy star Dwayne Bacon hasn't lost but all he wants to be is a winner |url=https://usatodayhss.com/2015/oak-hill-star-dwayne-bacon-hasnt-lost-but-all-he-wants-to-be-is-a-winner-dwayne-bacon-florida-state-dwayne-bacon-fsu |access-date=August 16, 2015 |publisher=USA Today High School Sports}} On September 5, 2014. Dwayne Bacon committed to [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] over offers from [[Oklahoma State Cowboys basketball|Oklahoma State]], [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]], and [[Auburn Tigers men's basketball|Auburn]].{{Cite web |last=Payne |first=Terrence |date=September 5, 2015 |title=Five-star small forward Dwayne Bacon commits to Florida State |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/college-basketball/news/five-star-small-forward-dwayne-bacon-commits-to-florida-state |access-date=August 16, 2015 |publisher=[[NBC Sports]]}} In his senior year at Oak Hill, Dwayne Bacon led Oak Hill to an undefeated regular season with a record of 45–0 and averaged 24.4 points per game, 4.4 rebounds per game, 3.4 assists per game, and 2.2 steals per game. He was ranked 14th on ESPN 100.{{Cite web |title=Dwayne Bacon – Recruiting – Player Profiles |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/168587 |access-date=May 8, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}} Bacon played for the Showtime Ballers AAU program based in Orlando for three seasons. ==College career== Bacon signed with [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] on September 5, 2015. As a freshman at Florida State, Bacon received the National Freshman of the week honors from CBS Sports on November 21. He was a three-time ACC rookie of the week (Nov 16, Dec 21 and 28). In his first career game Bacon had 23 points, 8 rebounds, 2 steals and 1 assist. Bacon achieved his first career win over [[Charleston Southern Buccaneers men's basketball|Charleston Southern]] with 20 points and 10 rebounds. He appeared in every game during the 2015–16 season for the Seminoles and averaged 15.8 points and 5.8 rebounds over 28.8 minutes per game. On March 23, Bacon announced via Twitter that he would test his draft status for the [[2016 NBA draft]]. He did not hire an agent and retained his amateur status and the ability to return to Florida State for the 2016–17 season.{{Cite magazine |date=March 22, 2017 |title=Florida State freshman Dwayne Bacon declares for NBA draft |url=https://www.si.com/college/2017/03/22/ap-bkc-florida-state-bacon |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]]}} However, on March 28 he announced he will return to college.{{Cite web |title=Florida State's Bacon withdraws from NBA draft consideration | NCAA Men's Basketball |url=http://collegebasketball.ap.org/node/856550 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160422152212/http://collegebasketball.ap.org/node/856550 |archive-date=April 22, 2016 |access-date=March 29, 2016}} During his sophomore season, Bacon was named a member of the All-ACC second team for his work with Florida State that season. After his team was eliminated from the [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2017 NCAA tournament]], Bacon declared for the [[2017 NBA draft]] (with a commitment that he'd sign with an agent soon afterward) on March 22, 2017. ==Professional career== ===Charlotte Hornets (2017–2020)=== On June 22, 2017, Bacon was selected by the [[New Orleans Pelicans]] with the 40th overall pick in the [[2017 NBA draft]]. He was later traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] on draft night.{{Cite web |date=June 23, 2017 |title=Pelicans Acquire Draft Rights to Frank Jackson |url=https://www.nba.com/pelicans/news/pelicans-acquire-draft-rights-frank-jackson |access-date=May 8, 2023 |publisher=[[National Basketball Association]]}} On July 6, he signed with the Hornets.{{Cite web |last=Wash |first=Quinton |date=July 6, 2017 |title=Hornets Sign Guard Dwayne Bacon |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/charlotte-hornets-sign-guard-dwayne-bacon |access-date=May 8, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} Bacon made his NBA debut on October 18, recording eight points, two rebounds and two assists in a 90–102 loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{Cite web |title=Charlotte Hornets vs Detroit Pistons Oct 18, 2017 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021700003 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} On November 3, he scored a season-high 18 points, alongside seven rebounds, in a 101–108 loss to the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web |title=Charlotte Hornets vs San Antonio Spurs Nov 3, 2017 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021700126 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} Bacon played in 53 games his rookie season and made six starts. He averaged 3.3 points and 2.3 rebounds per game. On March 26, 2019, Bacon scored a season-high 24 points, alongside six rebounds and three steals, in a 125–116 overtime win over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{Cite web |title=San Antonio Spurs vs Charlotte Hornets Mar 26, 2019 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021801107 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} During his sophomore season, Bacon only played in 43 games and made 13 starts due to a stint in the [[NBA G League]] with the Hornets' affiliate team, the [[Greensboro Swarm]]. However, his numbers improved statistically, with him averaging 7.3 points per game.{{Cite web |title=Hornets player review: Dwayne Bacon |url=https://www.atthehive.com/2019/5/6/18516399/charlotte-hornets-player-review-dwayne-bacon-two-way-player-improvement |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=SB Nation}} On November 2, 2019, Bacon scored a season-high 25 points, alongside six rebounds, two assists and two steals, in a 93–87 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{Cite web |title=Rozier, Hornets Hold Off Warriors 93–87 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021900083 |access-date=February 4, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}} During his third season, Bacon regressed statistically, averaging only 5.7 points per game. In June 2020, he stated that instead of staying with the Hornets, he would "go elsewhere."{{Cite web |title=2019–2020 Hornets report card: Dwayne Bacon |url=https://www.atthehive.com/2020/6/15/21289424/2019-2020-charlotte-hornets-report-card-dwayne-bacon |access-date=February 4, 2023 |website=SB Nation}} ===Orlando Magic (2020–2021)=== On November |publisher=National Basketball Association}} ===Panathinaikos (2022–2023)=== On October 21, 2022, Bacon signed a two-year deal (with several opt-out clauses for the club) with [[Panathinaikos B.C.|Panathinaikos]] of the [[Greek Basket League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].{{Cite web |date=October 21, 2022 |title=Dwayne Bacon signed with Panathinaikos |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1407947/dwayne-bacon-signed-with-panathinaikos/ |access-date=November 15, 2023 |website=Eurohoops.net}} On April 28, 2023, Bacon was prematurely released from the team in the middle of the [[Greek Basket League]] play-offs due to a series of disciplinary violations that the player had committed throughout the season.{{Cite web |first=Stavros |last=Barbarousis |date=April 27, 2023 |title=Dwayne Bacon and Panathinaikos are parting ways |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1495010/dwayne-bacon-and-panathinaikos-are-parting-ways/ |website=eurohoops.net|access-date=May 10, 2025}} In 27 EuroLeague games, Bacon averaged 16.6 points, 3.5 rebounds and 2 assists (with 1.3 turnovers), playing around 31 minutes per contest. Additionally, in 17 domestic league matches, he averaged 13.2 points, 3.9 rebounds and 2.3 assists, playing around 24 minutes per contest. ===Leones de Ponce (2024)=== On May 23, 2024, Bacon signed with the [[Leones de Ponce (basketball)|Leones de Ponce]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]].{{cite web |title=Dwayne Bacon se integra a los Leones de Ponce
